categories.name: Grooves
categories.blurb: Four starting points. Everything here is one string of mini-notation, with at most one function after it.

categories.name: Euclidean rhythms
categories.blurb: `sound(hits, steps, rotation)` spaces the hits as evenly as the steps allow. Many traditional rhythms fall out of it.

categories.name: Breaks and fills
categories.blurb: Sixteen-step breakbeats, and ways to vary them from bar to bar.

categories.name: Linear drumming
categories.blurb: Linear means no two drums are ever struck at the same moment. In Strudel that is a sequence with no commas in it: every step holds exactly one sound. Each grid has at most one hit per column.

categories.name: Dynamics and feel
categories.blurb: Volume and density do as much as the notes. These use `.gain()`, `.ply()` and chance.

categories.name: Polyrhythm and odd meters
categories.blurb: Layers that disagree about how long the bar is.

categories.name: Mini-notation shapes
categories.blurb: Rhythm and phrasing written inside the quotes, before any function is called.

categories.name: Degrees and scales
categories.blurb: Write numbers with `n()`, do arithmetic on them, and let `.scale()` turn the result into notes.

categories.name: Chords
categories.blurb: Two ways to get movement out of a chord progression.

categories.name: Layers and canons
categories.blurb: Copy the pattern, change the copy, play both.

categories.name: Time transforms
categories.blurb: Functions that rearrange when the notes happen, cycle by cycle.

categories.name: Chance
categories.blurb: Randomness that stays musical. Each roll shows one possible outcome; Strudel's random values are different every cycle.

snippets.name: Four on the floor
snippets.description: Commas stack layers inside one string. Kick on every beat, clap on two and four, and `[~ hh]*4` puts the hat on every offbeat.

snippets.name: Rock backbeat
snippets.description: Eighth-note hats, snare on two and four, and a kick that pushes into beat three with `[~ bd]`.

snippets.name: Boom bap with swing
snippets.description: `.swingBy(1/3, 4)` delays the second half of each beat to the triplet position. Straight code, lazy feel.
snippets.code:
s("bd ~ ~ bd ~ ~ bd ~, ~ sd ~ sd, hh*8")
  .swingBy(1/3, 4)

snippets.name: Half-time shuffle
snippets.description: Three slots per beat with the middle one silent gives the shuffle. One snare on beat three makes it half-time.

snippets.name: Tresillo
snippets.description: `bd(3,8)` spreads three kicks over eight steps as evenly as possible: 3 + 3 + 2. It sits under a plain backbeat.

snippets.name: Three euclids
snippets.description: Different hit counts and step counts on each voice. The third number rotates a pattern, here moving the rim off the downbeat.

snippets.name: Rotating rim
snippets.description: The rotation can be a pattern too. The same five-hit figure starts one step later every cycle.

snippets.name: Son clave
snippets.description: The 3-2 clave is a tresillo followed by two hits in the middle of the second half, so it fits in one short sequence.

snippets.name: Amen-style break
snippets.description: Kick and snare never land together in this break, so they share one sixteen-step sequence. Hats go in a second layer.
snippets.code: s("bd ~ bd ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ sd bd bd sd ~ ~ sd, hh*8")

snippets.name: Fill every fourth bar
snippets.description: `<sd!3 sd*4>` plays a single snare for three cycles and four quick ones on the fourth.

snippets.name: Two-step
snippets.description: The drum and bass skeleton: kick on one, snare on two, a late second kick, snare on four.

snippets.name: Travelling stutter
snippets.description: `.chunk(4, …)` picks one quarter of the bar per cycle and `.ply(2)` doubles every hit in it.
snippets.code:
s("bd ~ bd ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ sd bd bd sd ~ ~ sd")
  .chunk(4, x => x.ply(2))
snippets.base: s("bd ~ bd ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ sd bd bd sd ~ ~ sd")

snippets.name: Hats step aside
snippets.description: Take a backbeat and remove the hat wherever the kick or snare plays. What is left is one hit per sixteenth.
snippets.code: s("bd hh hh hh sd hh hh bd hh bd hh hh sd hh hh hh")

snippets.name: Ghosts in the gaps
snippets.description: The main line leaves every third sixteenth empty. A second layer drops quiet snares into exactly those holes, so the two still never collide.
snippets.code:
stack(
  s("bd hh ~ hh sd ~ hh bd ~ bd hh ~ sd hh ~ hh"),
  s("~ ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~ ~ sd ~").gain(.3)
)

snippets.name: Paradiddle funk
snippets.description: A paradiddle (RLRR LRLL) with the right hand on the hat and the left on the snare, and a kick taking the first note. The gain list accents the backbeat and ghosts the other snares.
snippets.code:
s("[bd sd hh hh sd hh sd sd]*2")
  .gain("[1 .3 .7 .7 1 .7 .3 .3]*2")

snippets.name: Threes over sixteenths
snippets.description: Hat, snare, kick is the classic three-note linear cell. `{…}%16` runs it at sixteen steps per cycle, so it crosses the barline and comes back around after three cycles.

snippets.name: Hand, hand, foot
snippets.description: A linear fill: two strokes with the hands, one with the kick, as triplets. Moving the hands from snare down the toms does the rest.
snippets.code: s("[sd sd bd] [ht ht bd] [mt mt bd] [lt lt bd]")

snippets.name: Rotate it
snippets.description: A linear pattern stays linear however you rotate it. `.iter(4)` starts the bar one beat later each cycle and gives four grooves from one line.
snippets.code:
s("bd hh hh sd hh bd sd hh bd hh sd hh hh sd bd hh")
  .iter(4)

snippets.name: Accented hats
snippets.description: A gain pattern per beat (loud, soft, medium, soft) turns sixteen identical hats into something that breathes.

snippets.name: Ghost notes
snippets.description: Keep the backbeat in one layer and put the quiet snares in another with low gain. The ghosts fill the space between kick and snare.

snippets.name: Hat rolls
snippets.description: `.ply()` repeats a hit inside its own step. Give it a pattern and only chosen hats turn into rolls, with a different roll on alternate bars.

snippets.name: Coin-flip hats
snippets.description: A question mark gives each hit a 50% chance of playing. The hat line is different every cycle while kick and snare hold still.

snippets.name: Three against four
snippets.description: Multiplying two voices by different numbers inside one cycle is all a polyrhythm needs.

snippets.name: Three-step hats, eight-step bar
snippets.description: Curly braces keep every layer at the step size of the first. The three-step hat figure drifts against the eight-step kick and snare, and realigns after three cycles.
snippets.code: s("{bd ~ sd ~ bd bd sd ~, hh hh oh}")

snippets.name: Seven in a bar
snippets.description: A cycle has no fixed meter. Write seven steps and you are in seven, here grouped 2 + 2 + 3.

snippets.name: Clapping phase
snippets.description: After Steve Reich's Clapping Music: the rim plays the clap's twelve-step pattern but starts one step later every cycle.
snippets.code:
s("cp cp cp ~ cp cp ~ cp ~ cp cp ~")
  .superimpose(x => x.iter(12).s("rim"))

snippets.name: Euclidean pairs
snippets.description: `(3,8)` spreads three hits evenly over eight steps. Put a `(5,8)` above it, rotated by two steps, and the two parts interlock.

snippets.name: Polymeter drift
snippets.description: Five notes read at eight steps per cycle. Each cycle starts on a different note, and the phrase lines up again after five cycles.

snippets.name: Nested alternation
snippets.description: Angle brackets pick one item per cycle. One line becomes a two-bar phrase whose second bar ends differently.

snippets.name: Stretch and repeat
snippets.description: `@3` holds a note for three steps, `!2` plays one twice. Seven units share the cycle, which gives a lopsided seven-feel.

snippets.name: One shape, two modes
snippets.description: Write the contour once as scale degrees, then alternate the scale underneath. The shape stays and the colour changes.

snippets.name: Diatonic sequence
snippets.description: Adding a slow pattern of offsets to the degrees walks the motif down the scale one step per cycle, staying in key.

snippets.name: Octave-jump bass
snippets.description: Three layers added together: steady eighths, a rhythm of octave leaps, and a root that moves every cycle.

snippets.name: Parallel triads
snippets.description: Adding the stack `[0,2,4]` puts a third and a fifth on every step. The scale decides which triads come out major or minor.

snippets.name: Arp by index
snippets.description: `.arp()` takes a pattern of chord-tone indices, so the picking order has its own rhythm, separate from the changes.

snippets.name: Voice-led comping
snippets.description: `.voicing()` turns chord symbols into close voicings and keeps the voices moving as little as possible. `.struct()` gives them a rhythm.

snippets.name: Echo a fifth up
snippets.description: `.off()` lays a shifted copy over the original. Shift it an eighth of a cycle and raise it four degrees for instant counterpoint.

snippets.name: Augmentation canon
snippets.description: The copy plays the same line at half speed, an octave up. A classical canon device in one call.

snippets.name: Echo staircase
snippets.description: `.echoWith()` hands each repeat its index. Use it to climb two degrees per echo and one note becomes a run.

snippets.name: Step phasing
snippets.description: The lower copy slips one more step behind each cycle, so the two lines drift apart in the manner of Steve Reich's phase pieces.

snippets.name: Rotating start
snippets.description: `.iter(4)` starts the phrase a quarter later each cycle. Four bars of variation from one bar of notes.

snippets.name: There and back
snippets.description: `.palindrome()` plays every second cycle backwards. Rests flip too, so the rhythm mirrors along with the melody.

snippets.name: Ratchets
snippets.description: `.ply()` repeats each note inside its own step. Pattern the amount and the line tightens from quarters to sixteenths.

snippets.name: Travelling octave
snippets.description: `.chunk(4, …)` applies a change to one quarter of the cycle, then moves to the next quarter. Here that quarter jumps up an octave.

snippets.name: Can't-miss random
snippets.description: `irand(8)` gives random whole numbers and `.segment(8)` samples it eight times a cycle. A pentatonic scale makes every outcome sound intended.

snippets.name: Perlin contour
snippets.description: `perlin` is smooth noise, so neighbouring samples sit close together. The result wanders in steps instead of leaping around.

snippets.name: Thinning
snippets.description: `.degradeBy(0.4)` drops about 40% of the notes at random. A busy line turns into a different sparse one every cycle.

snippets.name: Coin-flip steps
snippets.description: A pipe inside brackets chooses one option at random each cycle. Fix the downbeat and let the other steps vary.
